children: The European Union reached "substantial agreement" on a planned trade deal with the Philippines as the bloc's officials continue to look for closer economic ties with other countries.

Maros Sefcovic, the EU's top trade negotiator, said on Tuesday that both sides agreed to liberalize more than 94% of tariff lines covering more than 97% of trade in goods. "This is very good news, and a major opening for EU exporters who already sell over 8 billion euros [$9.17 billion] a year" to the Philippines in goods from machinery and medicines to pork and dairy, he said.
Sefcovic said the key parameters of a deal have been agreed on at a political level ahead of preparing a legal text that could be signed by both sides.
The commission said in a statement that the agreement would also cover rules on government procurement contracts, intellectual property, digital trade and sustainability agreements.

The EU trade chief said the deal would deliver real opportunities for businesses and also help diversify the bloc's supply chains. The commission--which oversees trade policy for the 27-member bloc--has been working to curb economic reliance on the U.S. and China by bolstering commercial ties with other countries.

In a joint statement issued on Tuesday, the commission said that Sefcovic and Philippine Secretary of Trade and Industry Cristina Roque had instructed their negotiating teams to finalize the agreement as soon as possible.

title: EU Reaches 'Substantial Agreement' on Philippines Trade Deal
